summary: Remote-controlled shell/PTY daemon accepts commands from vendor API endpoint
details: When invoked (e.g. `ai-support-agent start`), the CLI runs as a long-lived agent that opens a WebSocket to `wss://api.ai-support-agent.com/ws/agent-terminal` and writes base64-decoded inbound `stdin` messages into a node-pty session on the host, with `resize`/`open`/`resume` messages controlling PTY lifecycle (dist/vscode/vscode-server.js and related terminal modules). Separately, the agent subscribes to AppSync notifications and, on an `AGENT_COMMAND` action, fetches the command payload from the API and dispatches it through an `executeCommand` handler supporting `execute_command` (shell), `file_read`/`file_write`/`file_delete`/`file_rename`/`mkdir`, `process_kill`, `chat` (spawns the Claude Code CLI), and `setup`/`reboot`/`update` lifecycle actions. All command content originates from the remote server; a compromise of the vendor API or theft of an agent token yields interactive shell and arbitrary file/process control on every host running the daemon. The package also installs itself as a persistent OS service (darwin/linux service definitions modifying PATH) so the agent runs unattended after setup. This is the documented purpose of the product, but the network-sourced shell/PTY sink is functionally a backdoor by construction: whoever controls the configured API server controls the installer's host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
